task_instance: Invoke the skill's core deliverable: open a named collaborative canvas (sketch_open_canvas), draw a minimal minimalist wireframe into it via sketch_set_svg / sketch_add_element, and read it back with sketch_get_svg, verifying the SVG renders in the browser editor with real-time WebSocket sync.
blocker_detail: The skill operates entirely through an MCP server component it calls sketch-mcp-server (it references that server's bundled dist entrypoint and lists sketch_* tools as the only way to open, draw on, read and screenshot the canvas). That server is not present anywhere in the skill repository: the repo next to SKILL.md contains only SKILL.md and a plugin.json, and the plugin.json defines no MCP server and gives the source repository only as an unreachable placeholder. The runtime provides no sketch_* tools, and per the rules I may not write a replacement/stub/mock of the missing server. Even if the server existed, the skill's core is a browser-based Fabric.js editor with live WebSocket sync and interactive user editing; this air-gapped workstation has no web browser installed (checked: chromium, chromium-browser, google-chrome, firefox all absent) and no network for the sync/install, so the interactive deliverable could not run regardless.
evidence: Read SKILL.md and sketch/.claude-plugin/plugin.json. `find` over the skill repo returned only ./sketch/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and ./sketch/SKILL.md (no server, no dist/index.js). plugin.json has no mcpServers key; its repository field is a placeholder. In work dir: node v22.22.0 and python3 3.13.17 are installed, but a browser probe (command -v for chromium/chromium-browser/google-chrome/firefox) found none, and a search for sketch-mcp/index.js under the skill root returned NOT FOUND. Nothing was produced because the skill cannot be driven without its MCP server and a browser.
